clue.text: Show privates one after performance

definitions.meaning: two private soldiers in the US army, each a GI, side by side

indicators.note: the single letter for one is placed after the word for a performance

parts.note: a gig is a musician's performance
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A revue in which soldiers take turns on stage after the main act.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet here: 'privates' is GI twice over, and 'one after performance' builds the same letters from GIG plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerner and Loewe's musical, later a film, is named after its Parisian heroine.

clue.text: Poster girl's getting over old breathing restriction

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, abbreviated to ad

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name sits over and around the abbreviation for old, enclosing it

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name, here with its possessive s

explanation.surface: A poster girl's success is held back by an old breathing complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' puts the girl's name around O, making ENOIDS, after AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged lymph tissue at the back of the nose can block the airway, so these swellings restrict breathing.

clue.text: Judge is having to defend hostess

indicators.note: to defend is to surround and protect, so the answer is held within these clue words

explanation.surface: A judge has to stand up for a hostess in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to defend' signals letters hidden across 'Judge is having'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese woman trained to entertain male guests with conversation, music and dance is a professional hostess.

clue.text: Rising cheer welcoming politician's preparation to speak

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the reversed cheer contains the politician
in a down clue, rising means the word for a cheer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hurrah is a cheer
an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A rising cheer greets a politician as they get up to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the cheer upside down, as a down clue reads bottom to top, before 'welcoming' takes in the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud throat-clearing noise is what a pompous speaker makes before beginning, so it heralds speech.

clue.text: Sailor comes into fortune with plenty of 21

indicators.note: comes into means enters, so the sailor's letters go inside the fortune

parts.note: a pile is a fortune, as in making one's pile
OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor inherits a fortune and a full head of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is HAIR, so 'plenty of 21' means hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical and zoological term meaning covered in soft hairs, so thickly hirsute.

clue.text: Miss large equipment being erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, being erected means set upright, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Someone misses large equipment as it is put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being erected' turns LRIG upside down in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title for a young unmarried woman, so a lass or young woman.

clue.text: Cheat plays field, nicking diamonds and rupees

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, taking the diamonds into the rearranged word
plays means fools around with, so the letters of field are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
R is the abbreviation for rupees, Indian currency

explanation.surface: A cheat plays the field, pinching jewels and cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges FIELD to FIDLE, and 'nicking' puts D inside it to make FIDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or fraudster who works a dishonest racket is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Drink annually provided by one in cricket club

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, annually

indicators.note: in means the condition and the numeral sit inside the club's letters

parts.note: if means provided that
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricket club gets its annual drink supply from one member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, so 'Drink' can define an ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls the sea the drink, and this is the largest ocean.

clue.text: Top one of 15 is one of 15

definitions.meaning: 15 is CATS; the king of beasts is the top big cat
a rugby union side has fifteen players

explanation.surface: The leader of fifteen is still just one of the fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 points to the answer CATS, but the second 15 is just the number of a rugby union team.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is the king of the cats, and the British and Irish touring rugby side are called by its plural.

clue.text: Big game's excellent winger

parts.note: superb means excellent
an owl is a bird, a winged creature

explanation.surface: The big game's star is a brilliant wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a football player on the wing; here it is just a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual championship of American football is that sport's biggest fixture.

clue.text: Impresarios botch up records

indicators.note: to botch is to mess up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Showbusiness managers make a mess of their recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios finance and stage shows, which is what theatre backers who put on productions do.

clue.text: She showed some initiative in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round, so the part taken is read backwards
some means a part of the word initiative is taken

explanation.surface: A woman who took the lead in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ATIVE from 'initiative' and 'in revolution' turns it round. 'showed' is a link: the woman is a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón is the woman portrayed in the Lloyd Webber musical named after her nickname.

clue.text: Message held up in parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
held means kept inside, so the letters are found within parliament

explanation.surface: A message delayed in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' picks LIAME out of 'parliament' and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic note sent over a network is a kind of message.

clue.text: Device for electricians makes them more nervous

indicators.note: nervous means jittery, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A gadget that puts tradespeople on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures electrical resistance, a standard tool for wiring work.

clue.text: No introduction needed for elite competitors

indicators.note: no introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the gentry are the elite of society

explanation.surface: The best competitors need no introducing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No introduction needed' removes the G from GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The field of contestants in a race or show is collectively called its entrants list.

clue.text: Men in cabarets strip off

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the word for strip comes out of cabarets

parts.note: to bare is to strip

explanation.surface: Men at the cabaret take their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' looks like the stage action; it is BARE, removed from 'cabarets' by 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: In jazz slang a cat is a man or fellow, so cool cats are guys.

clue.text: Not at home during quiet quarter

indicators.note: during means within, so the word for absent goes inside the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
out means not at home

explanation.surface: Away from home during a quiet part of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one of the four compass points, and this is one of them.

clue.text: Vocalist enlists pair that should raise game

indicators.note: enlists means takes in, so the vocalist contains the pair

parts.note: a singer is a vocalist

explanation.surface: A singer recruits a duo who should lift their performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise game' sounds like improving; it means flushing birds for the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of spaniel is used to flush, or spring, game birds from cover.

clue.text: She's eliminated artist from unarmed combat

indicators.note: eliminated means removed, so the artist comes out of the martial art

parts.note: karate is a form of unarmed combat
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman has knocked an artist out of a martial-arts contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, as in the Shakespeare heroine of Kiss Me, Kate.

clue.text: Sort English news in Kentucky county

indicators.note: in means the run of pieces goes inside the state's letters

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
ilk means sort or kind
N stands for new, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Sorting English news in a Kentucky county.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a US county; the answer is an Irish one.
explanation.definitionFit: An inland county in the southeast of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Consumed about city vehicle offering many options

indicators.note: about means around, so the eaten word goes round the city and vehicle

parts.note: ate means consumed
LA is Los Angeles, a city
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Eating out in a city car with plenty to choose from.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu priced dish by dish lets the diner pick from many items rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Refrain in Switzerland or America

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: Holding back, whether in Switzerland or America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning abstain; it is the noun, a repeated part of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated section sung after each verse of a song is its burden.

clue.text: Boys now and then nurse sick goat

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the alternate letters contain the word for sick
now and then means every other letter of boys is taken

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Boys occasionally tend a sick goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now and then' takes B and Y from 'Boys', and 'nurse' wraps them round ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat is called by this name, as in the billy goat.

clue.text: New growth had damaged idol

parts.note: a bud is a plant's new growth

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of had are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh shoots have damaged a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue of the enlightened founder of a religion is worshipped as an idol.

clue.text: Pulled over lad running round with beak

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for pulled goes round the reversed lad

parts.note: in golf or cricket a pulled shot is hooked

indicators.note: running round means turned back, so the lad's word is reversed

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy pulled over while running round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled' is a golf or cricket shot curving off line, not a police stop; 'running round' turns the lad backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is slang for a nose, and an aquiline, curved nose suits this compound adjective.

clue.text: Shock personnel keeping fit

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the department contains the fitness letters

parts.note: HR is human resources, the personnel department
A1 means fit or first-rate, here written as letters

explanation.surface: Staff get a shock when kept fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is A1, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick mass of untidy locks on the head is called a shock.

clue.text: Pound for a book

definitions.meaning: the first name of the American poet Pound
a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Paying a pound for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist poet Pound shared his first name with the scribe whose Old Testament book follows Chronicles.

clue.text: Top that's hit in anger

definitions.meaning: the covering on top of a building
people hit the ceiling's outer covering when they explode with anger

explanation.surface: A lid that gets struck in fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a house is its covering, and to hit it is the idiom for losing one's temper.

clue.text: Burn fuel occasionally in entrance

indicators.note: in means the picked letters go inside the word for entrance

parts.note: to entrance is to rivet, hold spellbound

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of fuel is taken

explanation.surface: Burning fuel now and again in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is the Scots word for a stream, and 'entrance' is the verb meaning captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a small stream or brook.

clue.text: Spook horse in show with mike

indicators.note: in means the horse letter goes inside the show

parts.note: a panto is a pantomime, a British Christmas stage show
H is slang for heroin, horse
Mike is the radio alphabet's word for M

explanation.surface: A pantomime horse spooks someone on stage with a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British family Christmas show; 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A spook is a ghost or spectre, an apparition.
